page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-48-standardlssd is an x86_64 storage-optimized virtual machine tailored for intensive I/O operations and large in-memory working sets. The instance delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 378 GB of system memory, providing an allocation ratio of 7.88 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not included in this configuration.

Storage capability is anchored by 11,274 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity across three physical drives. This architecture provides high-bandwidth, low-latency disk access directly attached to the host, circumventing standard network-attached block storage overhead. Dedicated physical core scheduling ensures consistent compute availability without hypervisor contention.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a high memory-to-core ratio and direct NVMe storage optimizes density for heavy transactional workloads. The trade-off centers on the ephemeral nature of local NVMe storage, which requires operational architectures to implement application-level replication and snapshotting for data durability. In addition, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The hardware profile fits relational database management systems, distributed NoSQL datastores, massive analytics indexing nodes, and real-time caching deployments demanding both extensive random read/write throughput and high memory capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-48-standardlssd is a storage-optimized x86_64 virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 378 GB of system memory, achieving an allocation of 7.88 GB per core. The server integrates 11,274 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage distributed across three disks, bypassing typical network storage latencies for extreme throughput and low-latency I/O operations. Without dedicated GPUs and including zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is engineered specifically for dense compute and storage balance. Resource allocation efficiency is heightened by matching significant volatile memory with direct non-volatile scratch space, though workloads must account for the ephemeral nature of host-attached NVMe storage. This instance suits high-throughput transactional databases, distributed NoSQL clusters, real-time log ingestion systems, and large in-memory analytics workloads requiring substantial fast local scratch space.
